meta.title: Advanced Stem Cell Therapy: 3D-Bioprinted Brain-Like Transplants for Alzheimer's Disease-Like Dementia.

extracted_by: seed: Claude (Claude Code session), pending human review
summary: A soft gelatin/alginate/fibrinogen bioink was used to print hiPSC-derived neural progenitors into small dot-shaped hippocampal patches for transplantation. Transplants improved outcomes in a mouse model of Alzheimer's-like dementia.

formulations.stiffness_note: compressive modulus 1-4 kPa during culture; shear modulus <1 kPa
formulations.review_notes: Stiffness is reported as a 1-4 kPa range, so stiffness_kpa is left null. Extrusion was volume-controlled (1 mm3/s), not pressure-controlled.
formulations.name: GEL10: gelatin / alginate / fibrinogen
formulations.key_outcome: Viability 86.4% after printing and 77.0% at day 14; transplanted patches improved Alzheimer's-like dementia outcomes.

evidence.quote: The bioink (2.56% gelatin, 0.14% alginate, 0.57% fibrinogen) formed stably and mimicked brain tissue mechanics.
the medium concentration (6.67 × 10⁶ cells·mL−1) was selected for further study
needle inner diameter of 0.30 mm, printing speed of 5 mm·s−1, and extrusion speed of 1 mm3·s−1
demonstrating 86.38 ± 1.25% viability post‐printing that stabilized to 76.99 ± 1.59% by DAY 14
